html:
"Danube Bulgars" is the map's label, for 700, for the lands of the Bulgar state north of the lower Danube, in what is now Romania and Moldova.

The Bulgars were a Turkic-speaking steppe people. When the Khazars broke up their realm north of the Black Sea, a group led by Asparuh moved west to the Danube delta. In 680 they beat a Byzantine army, and in 681 the Byzantine Empire recognised their state, the First Bulgarian Empire. They settled south of the river and ruled the Slavs there from Pliska, while also holding wide lands to the north.

Over the next two centuries the Bulgar elite took up the Slavic speech of their subjects, and in 864 Khan Boris accepted Christianity; see Conversion of Bulgaria. Bulgarian control north of the Danube lasted, with breaks, until the Magyars and then the Pechenegs took over the steppe.
sum: "Danube Bulgars" is the map's label, for 700, for the lands of the Bulgar state north of the lower Danube, in what is now Romania and Moldova.
